title: Count land regions
prompt:
grid is a map made of equal-length strings: "#" is land and "." is water. Land cells that touch up, down, left or right belong to the same region (diagonals do not connect). Return the number of regions.

- 0 to 300 rows and 1 to 300 columns.
- Use an explicit stack or queue: a recursive search can exceed the call stack on a 300×300 map.
hints: Each region is a connected component of land cells. How do you count components?
Scan every cell. When you find unvisited land, you have found a new region.
Flood-fill from that cell with a stack, marking every connected land cell visited, so later scans skip it.

solution.explanation: Every unvisited land cell found by the outer scan starts a new region; an iterative DFS then marks its whole component. Each cell is marked once, so total work is linear in the grid size.

complexity.notes: Union-find gives the same count and also supports adding land cells one at a time.

followUps: Land is added one cell at a time; report the region count after each addition.
